answer: At Pier 4's night desk, a barge dispatcher who wants a grain slot must place one opal glass token, etched with the hull number, on the clerk's scale for 14 seconds until the tide board stamps a wet-ink serial. A second watcher later weighs the same token (it must stay within 0.3 g of 41.6 g), matches the serial to camera stills of hatch #7, and checks that the ink smear leans left. If the scale never settles, the tide board prints no serial, or two stills disagree by more than 20 seconds, the deposit burns and a ripple of exclusion bars that hull from the grain board for 11 cycles.
